questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the CAP theorem?

options.text: Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance can all be achieved simultaneously.
Consistency and Partition tolerance can be achieved at the expense of Availability.
You can only guarantee two of the three properties at any time.
Partition tolerance is irrelevant to distributed systems.

questions.explanation: CAP states that a distributed system can satisfy at most two of Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance simultaneously.

questions.prompt: In an eventually consistent system, a client that writes a value and immediately reads it from a different replica may see what?

options.text: Either the old or new value depending on replication lag.
The system will throw an error.

questions.explanation: Replication lag can cause a stale read; eventual consistency only guarantees convergence over time.

questions.prompt: In Paxos, which role is responsible for collecting votes and deciding the chosen value?
questions.explanation: Acceptors receive proposals and vote; the value that receives a majority of votes is chosen.

questions.prompt: Which failure mode is most likely when a network partition splits a cluster of nodes?

options.text: All nodes lose connectivity to each other.
Some nodes can still communicate within their partition.

questions.explanation: A partition isolates subsets of nodes; nodes inside the same partition can still talk to each other.
